assumption_register.assumption: Each RAX generic hart may be given a distinct 4096-byte bootstrap stack page at the end of mapped RAM

assumption_register.falsification_probe: Stack aliases another hart, unmapped RAM or image bytes

assumption_register.assumption: Existing execution snapshot can encode every generic hart online and its scheduler cursor without a wire change

assumption_register.stress_test: Paused-before-work one/two/four-hart files and no reinitialization on resume
assumption_register.falsification_probe: Saved runnable mask/cursor changes or secondary instructions fail to continue
assumption_register.qualification: Actual source-free one/two/four-hart save/load, preserved multi-hart nonzero cursor/online/private contexts and new work after resume

bounded_scope.finding: Generic RISC-V CLINT/PLIC/VM-clock/SBI/platform replay remain required for full SMP; current bridge handles UART only
Remaining A32 controls/admission, full backend/private/in-flight profiles, native MMIO/IRQ and physical Intel qualification remain required
Legacy zero-based RAM and 4 GiB padding retained; this is a RAX bare-metal convention with 4096-byte bootstrap pages, not Linux/SBI/DTB boot qualification

One untraced QEMU 2-hart run timed out; traced repeat passed. Exact cause unknown. All 1/2/4 common-byte programs passed with explicit icount scheduling; no cycle-accuracy or unconstrained-QEMU success claim

Baseline upstream CI at 6d6342238 has Linux x86 native JIT verification divergence and a Windows fresh native registry replay mismatch. Root causes remain unknown; neither run contains this pending startup group. Linux ARM64 job separately received a runner shutdown signal.
Read-only host backing regressions execute on Unix. Windows host protection and general ELF symbol/relocation/ABI profiles are not qualified by these tests.
